instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt, bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.
Meanwhile, cut the onion into chunks. Put them in a small saucepan with 12 of the cashews, cover with water and boil for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Drain, then blend the onion and cashews with 3 tbsp water until smooth. Scrape the paste into a bowl.

Cut the potato into 1/2-inch pieces, dice the carrot, chop the beans into 1-inch pieces and cut the cauliflower into small florets. Fill the same saucepan with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil.
Add the potato, carrot and beans and cook for 5 minutes. Add the cauliflower and peas and cook for 2 minutes. Drain well. The vegetables should be tender but not mushy.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Chop the 6 remaining cashews, slice the almonds and cook them for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden. Add the raisins for 20 seconds, until they puff. Transfer all of it to a small bowl.
Cut the paneer into 3/4-inch cubes. Add them to the skillet and cook for 1 minute on each side, until pale golden. Transfer them to a plate.

Add the last 2 tbsp oil to the skillet over medium heat. Add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Grate in the ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and cashew paste. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the pan.

Stir in the chili powder, turmeric, coriander, garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 1 minute. Pour in 1 cup water, bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly thick.
Add the cooked vegetables and the pineapple, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, stir the cream with 2 tbsp of the hot gravy. Turn off the heat, then stir the cream into the pan so it doesn't split.
Fold in the paneer. Top with the fried nuts and raisins, the pomegranate arils and chopped cilantro. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes leads (5.0 from 64 ratings): an onion and cashew paste gravy, vegetables cooked separately and added at the end, and fried nuts, raisins and paneer folded in last. Cream is stirred in off the heat with a spoonful of hot gravy so it doesn't split. The optional chilies and rose water were left out to keep it mild.
